book_title: The Big Onion Guide to New York City: Ten Historic Tours
author: Seth I. Kamil and Eric Wakin (foreword by Kenneth T. Jackson)
source_file: The Big Onion Guide to New York City Ten Historic Tours (Seth I. Kamil, Eric Wakin, Kenneth Jackson) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf
extraction_note: Historian-led walking-tour guide (Big Onion Walking Tours / Columbia). Chunked at the natural per-tour chapter level: the 10 self-guided historic tours, each a turn-by-turn route (Start: transit + directions, then numbered/inline stops with deep historical narrative and addresses; the ➢ glyph marks walking directions). EXTRACTION CAVEAT: the PDF sets digits and small-caps in Adobe Expert fonts (FournierExpertMT) encoded in the private-use range U+F700-U+F7FF with no ToUnicode map, so plain pdftotext silently DROPS EVERY DIGIT (dates, addresses) -- catastrophic for a historical guide. Extracted instead via scripts/extract_pua_pdf.py (PyMuPDF + deterministic ASCII = codepoint - 0xF700 remap + fi/fl ligature expansion); 608-1611 digits/chunk recovered. Excluded as non-tour content: front matter (title, copyright, Introduction, About Big Onion) and back matter (Sources bibliography pp.382+, About the Contributors, Index). .cleaned.txt == .txt (strip_pdf_artifacts found no map-label artifacts).

chunks.section_title: Wall Street: The Architecture of Capitalism
chunks.summary: Wall Street tour: Bowling Green, the Custom House, Fraunces Tavern, Federal Hall, Trinity Church, the NYSE, the wall of New Amsterdam, the financial district's architecture and history of capitalism.

chunks.section_title: The Lower East Side: Immigrant New York
chunks.summary: Lower East Side immigrant tour: tenements, the Eldridge Street Synagogue, Orchard Street, German/Jewish/Irish/Italian/Chinese waves of settlement, sweatshops, settlement houses, and immigrant institutions.

chunks.section_title: Greenwich Village: A Gay and Lesbian History
chunks.summary: Greenwich Village LGBTQ history tour across the East and West Villages: the Stonewall Inn, Christopher Street, bohemian and queer landmarks, and the historical and contemporary gay and lesbian worlds of the Village.

chunks.section_title: Four Squares: Union Square, Stuyvesant Square, Gramercy Park, and Madison Square
chunks.summary: Four Squares tour from Fourteenth to Twenty-third Street: Union Square, Stuyvesant Square, Gramercy Park, and Madison Square -- commercial and residential Manhattan, labor history, mansions, and the Flatiron.

chunks.section_title: The Brooklyn Bridge: A Walk from Brooklyn Heights to City Hall
chunks.summary: Brooklyn Bridge tour from Brooklyn Borough Hall through Brooklyn Heights (Plymouth Church, the Promenade, brownstones) across the bridge to City Hall; the Roeblings, the Beecher trial, and consolidation.

chunks.section_title: Central Park: New York City's Largest Work of Art
chunks.summary: Central Park tour from Columbus Circle: Olmsted and Vaux's design, the Mall, Bethesda Terrace, the Ramble, Seneca Village, the Reservoir, and the park as a democratic landscape and engineered work of art.

chunks.section_title: The Upper East Side: Manhattan's "Gold Coast"
chunks.summary: Upper East Side 'Gold Coast' tour: Fifth Avenue mansions and Museum Mile, the Frick, Carnegie and Vanderbilt wealth, Park and Madison Avenues, and the social history beneath the myth of monolithic wealth.
Historic Harlem tour: the Harlem Renaissance, the Apollo Theater, Striver's Row, Abyssinian Baptist Church, 125th Street, and Harlem as the cultural and political capital of African American life.
Green-Wood Cemetery tour: the rural/garden cemetery movement, notable interments (Currier, Beecher, Tweed, Steinway, Morse), monuments and mausoleums, and the cemetery as proto-park in Brooklyn.

chunks.section_title: The Other Boroughs: A Driving Tour
chunks.summary: Driving tour of Staten Island, the Bronx, and Queens: Staten Island's St. George and historic Richmond, the Bronx (Grand Concourse, Yankee Stadium, Woodlawn), and Queens landmarks, linked by turn-by-turn driving directions.
